title: Return Statement Mistakes
summary: return must be the LAST statement of its block — code after it is dead; returning inside a nested function returns from THAT function; forgetting return gives nil. Module returns are their own gotcha (see module-return-mistakes).

explanation.whatItIs: Return has strict placement rules; breaking them yields dead code, wrong-level exits, or silent nils.
explanation.whyItExists: A block ends at return — anything after can never run, so Luau forbids it syntactically (mostly) and nil-fills omissions.
symptoms: Guard returns accidentally ending the outer function (nested function boundary confusion)
Functions returning nil because no return was written on some path
explanation.fix: Place returns last in their block; make every logical path return explicitly; remember function boundaries when writing guards inside callbacks.
tips: Guard clauses first, main logic after — early returns shine
Multiple returns: return a, b — callers pick what they need
Strict mode flags missing return paths on typed functions
commonMistakes: Returning from a Connect callback thinking it stops the outer function
If/else where only one branch returns — other branch yields nil

examples.title: Three classic slips
examples.code:
-- ❌ Dead code (Luau actually errors on this):
-- return 5
-- print("never")

-- ❌ Return in the wrong function:
local function outer()
    part.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
        return        -- exits the CALLBACK, not outer!
    end)
    print("this still runs")
end

-- ❌ Missing path:
local function classify(n)
    if n > 0 then
        return "positive"
    end
    -- n <= 0 falls through → nil!
end

-- ✅ Every path:
local function classifySafe(n)
    if n > 0 then return "positive" end
    return "zero or negative"
end
